boot.evidence: CI kernel+stub boots the docker flow via the daemon to WEB_UP_MARKER in ~40 s (COW boot, clean poweroff at stop).

c3_inbound_throughput.evidence: RESOLVED -- the 20261029-cap12 'gvproxy-bess-ok banner' anomaly was a port collision with the image's own demo web container (docker-init.sh starts it on guest 8123; its page content is literally 'gvproxy-bess-ok', 15 bytes; the binary gvproxy does not contain the string). With the test container on a DISTINCT published port (8124:80), the inbound path phone->gvproxy->bess->guest->dockerDNAT->container transferred 25165824 bytes twice: 3 s (~8.0 MB/s) and 2 s (~12 MB/s floor). Pull baseline from cap12 stands (alpine 29-33 s fresh).

c3_pull_baseline.evidence: See 20261029-cap12-c3-network.json: fresh alpine:3.19 29 s, alpine:3.20 33 s, manifest-only busybox:1.36 10 s (bess path, registry latency included).

observed.web_container_port: 0.0.0.0:8123->80/tcp (docker-init.sh demo, restart policy 'no', started by init script)
observed.resolution: port 8123 collision; inbound exposure path never broken

known_limits_observed: the docker-init.sh demo web container owns guest port 8123 on every boot -- tests must use other ports
notes: C3 closed: throughput measured on both directions of interest; the earlier open issue was a self-inflicted test collision, not a gvproxy regression. Cross-check: 'strings' on the gvproxy binary contains no 'gvproxy-bess-ok'.
